messages:
sam: Heads-up — after the FP8/INT8 mixed rollout to the 'fast-kernel' path we started seeing tail perf regressions on multi-request bursts (batch >= 8). Profiling attached in-thread, need opinions on whether this is calibration or kernel routing causing thrash.

anya: Can you paste the perf numbers? is this latency tail or throughput drop? :thinking_face:  

sam: Throughput drop primarily; 5–12% tokens/sec reduction on the 3B model under realistic traffic (seq 512 avg). Latency p95 is slightly worse when requests are heterogeneous lengths. Quick snippet from perf-bot: 
```
perf-bot: model=redwood-3b, config=fp8-mix, batch=8, baseline=124k tok/s, current=113k tok/s, delta=-8.87%
kernel-switches per 100k tok: baseline=3, current=18
KV cache misses %: baseline=0.7, current=2.9
```

mike: Those kernel-switch counts look suspicious. Could be we trigger a fallback to INT8/4-bit kernels for certain layers when calibration bins overflow. That results in extra memcpy + format conversion.

jia: Agree. I also wonder if the calibration dataset includes too many long-tail outliers (super long prompts, many rare tokens) which skew per-channel scales, forcing some layers into pathological ranges. How did we pick the calib set?

sam: We used the usual 2k sample scraped from public docs + logs (mix: 60% chat, 20% instructions, 20% long-form). No explicit trimming other than dedupe.

lucy: Per-channel vs per-tensor decision matters here. Per-channel tends to preserve accuracy but increases calibration sensitivity. If one channel sees a rare outlier token, its scale explodes and kernel selection might choose a slower path.

anya: Do we have evidence calibration is the root cause vs batching heuristics/KV cache alignment? Could be batching groups different seq lengths that break continuous KV caching and cause higher memory churn so kernels do extra work.

sam: Good point. I ran a controlled micro-bench: homogeneous requests (all seq=512) vs mixed (random 16..1024). Homogeneous: current ~= baseline. Mixed: current drops ~10%. So mixing seq lengths amplifies it. Profiling shows extra kernel transitions in mixed case.

mike: That aligns with routing logic: we select kernel variant based on sequence length distribution and quantization profile. If per-request quant stats vary, we recompile/select different kernel -> thrash. We should stabilize kernel selection by making calibration output less noisy across typical distribution.

jia: Proposed mitigation ideas: 1) Outlier trimming during calibration (e.g., remove top/bottom 0.5% per-channel samples), 2) Stratified sampling by seq length and prompt type to avoid overrepresenting long docs, 3) Use per-tensor when variance low and per-channel when justified by accuracy delta.

lucy: +1 for stratified sampling. Also consider storing two calibration profiles: a 'fast-stable' profile with clipped scales and a 'high-precision' profile. Router can pick the fast profile for noisy/mixed batches.

sam: I tried a quick experiment: trimmed top 1% per-channel and forced channel clamps at 8-bit-equivalent clip. Result: kernel-switches dropped from 18 -> 4 and throughput recovered ~6%. Accuracy delta (eval set) small: +0.3% perplexity change on long-form eval.

perf-bot: quick-run: calib-command used: 
```
./calibrate --model redwood-3b --method per_channel --samples 2000 --outlier-trim 0.01 --stratify seq_len,prompt_type --emit-profile fast
```

anya: Nice. Can you share the script or the filter logic? People will want to reproduce. Also what's the perf cost of using per-tensor fallback?

sam: Filter is naive MAD-based clipping: compute median and MAD per-channel, drop samples > median + 6*MAD. I can push the script. Per-tensor fallback is slightly faster on kernel path selection (fewer variants) but loses a small accuracy edge on some attention matrices.

mike: We should be careful tuning MAD multiplier. Too aggressive and we bias scales downward, maybe hurting rare-token fidelity. Perhaps use asymmetric clipping: clip positive outliers stronger than negatives. Rare tokens often create positive spikes.

jia: Also worth exploring calibration with synthetic prefixes to exercise KV cache hot paths. If our dataset lacks typical prefix patterns, KV cache alignment won't be tested and quant stats will be off.

lucy: Agree. Add synthetic conversational prefixes sampled from live logs (anonymized) to better match routing conditions. Also test with our batching heuristic that groups by seq_len buckets. If current heuristic mixes wide ranges in a bucket, that will still trigger cache churn.

sam: Action items: 
- sam: open PR with trimming script + reproduce commands (I'll include the MAD params and stratify config).
- mike: add a kernel-selection guard that prevents switching more than once per batch window (simple debounce).
- jia: produce a calibration sampling recipe that includes synthetic prefixes + stratification.
- lucy: run a canary with dual-profile routing (fast vs precise) and report perf/quality tradeoffs.

anya: Sounds good. One more ask: include a small flamegraph or perf trace in the PR so infra can inspect memcpy spikes. Those usually give the smoking gun.

sam: Will do. Putting preliminary numbers & the script in the PR shortly. Thanks all. :rocket: 

perf-bot: note: created issue #4521 (calib-sampler-protocol) and linked to thread.
